quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Park without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should park at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is determined by body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how quickly the alcohol is consumed. It is never safe to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated if their blood alcohol content (BAC) is at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is considered intoxicated. Intoxicated people cannot operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Motorcycles have the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic at:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles. Motorcyclists must be careful when approaching intersections.

questions.question: An engine will seize if:

options.text: The tires are not inflated properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when there is not enough oil. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed carefully. Always slow down when approaching an emergency scene.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT give you the best protection if it is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A helmet provides the best protection if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
The truck is completely behind you.
You feel you have enough space between you and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing a truck, only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must swerve and brake to avoid a hazard, separate the actions. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Always look through a turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Your rear wheel locks up while stopping on dry pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on dry pavement, you can keep it locked. Your motorcycle will stay stable and under control as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: When riding with a group, when should you NOT use a staggered formation?

options.text: When entering or exiting a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when entering or exiting a highway, riding in curves, or turning. Use a staggered formation at other times.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle. What is the rule?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Show a narrow view behind you.
Show a wide view behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a wide view behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. Objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex ones.

questions.question: What about the oily strip in the center of a lane?

options.text: Only ride on it if sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It has good traction unless it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has good traction unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip usually has enough traction for safe riding, except when it rains. The strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle respond with a passenger when turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. With the added weight, your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. Do not ride in the center of the lane. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle towing a trailer needs more stopping distance. The extra weight means the motorcycle takes longer to stop.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through each turn by turning only your head. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and move slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Drivers of larger vehicles may not correctly understand your speed and position.
